records.words: I know this page from my last visit. The landowner’s due is grain; I learned that. Now there is a new first sentence about a spoken answer during visits. I read it twice: “This uses the original grain rules and local people, instead of the other editions below.” Reread 1. Original rules, editions? I do not know which edition I am in. I leave the boxes alone and press Resume as I was told. New concepts, 3: spoken answer during visits, editions, original grain rules.
Resume, as prepared.
Last time I read too long and the rain came. Time is moving, so I call at once and read afterwards.
The big screen is pleasant and the text is readable. Now the screen says replies are at the houses. Kavak has a little circle, so I go there first. Still two days before rain this time.
The same sentence about the call expiring that stopped me last time. Now I just let it pass: it means I cannot call this house twice. Last time I never pressed Visit. This time I do.
I am walking. The clock stays at 07:30 while I read here, so I go back to the notebook to let the walk happen.
I wait for the walk, without Skip.
Five came! That is much better than last time. Zehra will come after her own barley; that is fair, she has her own family. I will not insist. I am at Kavak now, so I open it to hear them.
Say: I came to listen. That is what I would say as a new steward. I like that it is a plain sentence.
I said my words but I see no answer from them yet. Maybe it comes with time. I go back to the notebook.

Much better than last time: I called early, five people came, and I visited Kavak and said I came to listen. But the clock has stayed at 08:00. It says time moves slowly while a decision remains open. Is Zehra my open decision? I do not want to insist. New concepts, 6: replies at houses, walking minutes, Say during a visit, came/delayed/refused with names, Hold to insist, slowdown while a decision is open.
I wait to see if the slow time moves at all.
Ten came, seven will come after their own barley. Nobody refused. The Kavak overseer says sit down if you are staying. That is warm. I look whether they answered my words.
My words are gone and no answer is shown. A little disappointing. I open About to know who lives here.
The overseer has the only glass window, a nice detail. My record says I sat with them. The your guess lines are my own guesses, I think. I go back and let the visit finish.
Half an hour of game time per half minute of mine. The rain is two days away; at this speed I would sit here all evening. I have a concrete question: what does Skip do, and is it safe? I open the i.

The help is plain and I understood it on first reading: refusals, insisting, the grain bar. But it does not tell me what Skip does, and only 5 of 360 measures are cut while ten people work. I am interested but worried it is slow. New concepts, 6: threshing from 5 August, collecting household shares from 9 August, reducing a household payment, neighbours noticing, grain bar parts, knocks at the door.
I try Skip once, because waiting half a minute for half an hour is too slow for me. Its button says skip to the next event, so I hope it stops when something happens.
Skip is grey now. I wait to see what it brings.
Since I pressed Skip, the clock has not moved at all. Did Skip stop time? I wait longer.
I am home, 14 came. Skip is still grey; I do not know why. Çoban had a black dot first, maybe something waits there. I visit them too; the overseer said some houses listen only if you visit.
“Who will feed my family while I cut his barley?” That I understand completely. I will not insist. I go to sit with Zehra’s house instead.
Walking to Çoban.
I have arrived at Çoban. I open it to speak.
Again only one thing to say. I came to listen. It fits here even better, after her question about feeding her family.

Again my words show and nobody answers me. The first page promised a spoken answer during visits; where is it? Zehra asked who will feed her family. Maybe Send grain is my answer. I look what it asks first.

Oh! I only wanted to look, and it sent the grain at once. No question, no amount. I do not mind giving to Zehra, but I did not decide it. How much did I give? The rider will count it as missing. I feel a little tricked. New concepts, 1: gifts recorded in the ledger.
I look in the ledger to see how much I gave.
The ledger button is not here in the house view; I use the rain bar at the top, which says it opens the ledger.
The ledger is a clear table, I like it. 15 cut, 350 in the field. But it does not say how much I gave Zehra. It said the gift is recorded in the ledger; I do not see it.

The clock has stood at 10:30 for half a minute, though nothing is open. Sometimes time moves, sometimes not. I am waiting, but for what? Now the requested layout check: I switch to the phone size briefly.
Layout check on the phone: the map is very small, and the status line is cut off with three dots. The red Skip is big. Zehra is gone from the list; 15 came now. Yusuf says Come in. I open Çoban.

End of the phone layout check at 304 s, back to the wide screen. On the phone Çoban shows Yusuf: “Come in.” Only that. Is “Come in” the spoken answer? It answers my arrival, not my words. Zehra came to work after my grain, I think, but the game does not say why.
Waiting to walk home.

Yusuf: “Tell the landowner we are grateful. Or thank God for us instead.” I smiled; a proud man, a little sharp. These people feel real. But I mostly wait for half a minute at a time, and I have one thing to say at every house.
While I walk home I look at Other orders, in case there is something useful to do instead of waiting.
Both orders are grey, but each says plainly why. Fine. Nothing to do but visit and wait. New concept, 1: writing to the landowner for grain.
Ten minutes of walking takes me a whole real minute. I try Skip again; I am getting a little bored of waiting.
Home. Skip did not seem faster; it is grey again. Dere has a red dot on the phone picture, so maybe they need me. I open Dere.
Same polite delay. I visit Dere; it worked with Zehra after I sat with them and gave grain.
Walking to Dere.
Arrived at Dere.
This time I only listen and do not give grain. I want to see if listening alone changes anything.
Who lives here?
Two people by the stream, empty ox stall, low jars. Poor family. I feel I should give them grain, but I wait to see if listening is enough. Still no spoken answer to my words.

Dere says “Say what you came to say.” But I already said it, half an hour ago! The answer comes after my words and sounds like it came before. I do not feel heard. I wait half a minute, read one line, wait again. I am getting bored.
Maybe I can say something now that they asked.
They ask me to say what I came to say, and my only words are used up. So I answer with grain; their jars are low. This time I choose it knowingly.

Nine minutes, and the game day has gone from 7 to 2 in the afternoon. I have three buttons per house and the same one sentence each time. Dere has not even answered my grain. I understand everything now, but there is mostly waiting. I would like to stop here. I keep going because I set the time aside.

“That is kind of you. We’ll keep it for spring.” And the Dere person came to work: 16 came. That warmed me. So: sit, give, and they come. The wish to leave is smaller now, though the pattern is clear. Next I will try Tepe, which has three people waiting.
19 came now. Home again. Tepe next.
Visit Tepe.
Walking to Tepe.
At Tepe. One of them already came, 20 now.
Same words again. I would like a second thing to say, like asking about their own harvest.
The son spends more time at the coffeehouse than in the fields. Ha, I know families like that. I do not give grain here; I only listened. Let me see if they come anyway.
22 came now, 5 delayed, nobody refused. Tepe says “Sit down.” Things are going well in a quiet way. I like the people but the rhythm is slow: press three buttons, wait a minute and a half.
How is the harvest going? I check the ledger.

The granary went from 24 to 18; so my two gifts were about 3 each. I had to work that out myself. 70 cut, 290 still in the field, and the rain comes the day after tomorrow. I am worried we will not finish, but I do not know what else I can do except visit.
Still at Tepe; waiting to leave.
Tepe’s people came too, 24 now, with only listening, no grain. Good. So listening is enough sometimes. Only Kuyucu and Demirci remain. I will visit Demirci next.
Home. Demirci now.
Walking to Demirci.
At Demirci.
I came to listen, the fifth time.
Same routine. I go back and wait for their answer.
Demirci: “We weren’t expecting you.” Each house greets me with one line, a little different, and that is nice. But it is the same visit five times. Most of my time is waiting.
One more wait to see whether Demirci comes.

This time I understood what to do: call early, visit, listen, sometimes give grain. 24 people came and nobody refused, and I liked Yusuf and the Dere family. But after fifteen minutes it is still the first day, and every visit is the same three buttons and a minute of waiting. I stop here. I would close it, not leave it running. I would come back another evening only if the days went faster when nothing is happening and I had more than one thing to say.
After stopping: local Feedback inspection.
I choose I am stopping. I will not type or submit.

After stopping I chose I am stopping in Feedback. It became pressed and put I am stopping into the note box itself. I typed nothing and did not submit. Feedback and menu are familiar from last time; no new concepts. The browser is no longer needed.

records.source: Post-stop report section3; retrospective, not a measured contemporaneous record. May repeat raw words.
